create.name: Chinmaya International Foundation
create.bio:
Chinmaya International Foundation, known as CIF, is the research and study centre of the worldwide Chinmaya Mission, set up in 1989 to carry out Swami Chinmayananda's hope of linking India's classical learning with modern seekers. It lives at Adi Sankara Nilayam in the village of Veliyanad in Kerala's Ernakulam district, the house honoured as the maternal birthplace of Adi Shankaracharya, on ten green acres with old temple shrines and lotus ponds. Alongside Sanskrit research and the care of palm-leaf manuscripts, it teaches Advaita Vedanta, the Bhagavad Gita and the Upanishads.

Much of that teaching reaches people at home: the foundation runs online and postal study courses on the Gita, the Upanishads, Vedanta and Sanskrit, which it says have drawn more than fifteen thousand students. On campus it holds residential camps on single texts such as the Saundarya Lahari or the Shiva Mahimna Stotram, led by Chinmaya Mission swamis and scholars, and a seven-week immersive course on the Gita. Its Chinfo Channel, running since 2012, carries long discourse series on the Upanishads and the Bhagavatam, guided meditations drawn from the Upanishads, and festival observances streamed from the ashram.

courses.title: Gita Panchamrit: Echoes of the Absolute
courses.description: A residential camp at the Veliyanad campus led by Prof. Gauri Mahulikar, reading five verses of the Bhagavad Gita through the commentaries of five classical teachers, from Shankara and Ramanuja to Jnaneshvar.
courses.price: Shared Non AC Accommodation: ₹4800 | US$ 110; Shared AC Accommodation: ₹7200 | US$ 160

courses.title: Mahashivarathri Spiritual Retreat 2027
courses.description: Five days at Adi Sankara Nilayam around the night of Mahashivaratri, with discourses in Hindi by Swami Advaitananda Saraswati on the Shiv Mahimna Stotram, satsang and devotion.

courses.title: Saundarya Lahari Camp 6
courses.description: A residential retreat with Swami Sharadananda Sarasvati on the later verses of Shankara's hymn to the Divine Mother, combining chanting, guided study, silence and meditation in the rhythm of ashram life.
courses.price: For AC Accommodation: ₹9600 | US$ 215; For Non AC Accommodation: ₹6400 | US$ 145

courses.title: Bhagavad Gita Immersive
courses.description: A 48-day residential study of the whole Gita at the campus with Swami Advayananda, run with Chinmaya Vishwa Vidyapeeth, which certifies the programme.

courses.title: Bhagavad Gita Course - Online Mode
courses.description: A fifteen-month home-study course of thirty lessons and questionnaires covering the full Gita, written by Swami Tejomayananda and joining textual study with contemplation.

courses.title: Kena Upanishad (Shankara bhashya)
courses.description: A ten-lesson study of the Kena Upanishad with Shankara's commentary, taught by Br. Ved Chaitanya, on consciousness as the reality behind thought and perception.

sprint.tier_evidence: YouTube 85,700 subscribers (YouTube Data API, 10 Nov 2026); no other counts read → ~86k → local_hero. Published figure: 15,000+ students on its courses (about-cif page), for information only.
flags: Teachers file empty: none of the swamis and scholars on the channel (Swami Advayananda, Swami Swaroopananda, Swami Sharadananda, Br. Ved Chaitanya, Prof. Gauri Mahulikar) is on Spiritpedia. Possible future listings: Swami Swaroopananda, Swami Advayananda.
Tier borderline: 85,700 YouTube subscribers (80k–150k band); the foundation also publishes 15,000+ course students. Possible override by published student counts; not raised.
office@chinfo.org is the foundation's general office inbox.
Veliyanad is a village (Ernakulam district, Kerala); recorded as published.
Channel is also partly academic (Sanskrit drama lectures, grammar sessions); only spiritual-teaching videos chosen.
Prices on the Gita Panchamrit and Saundarya Lahari pages copied as published; other course pages show several prices from related-course cards, so 'Contact for pricing' used.
left_out: Website's 'Indian management' and Vedic Mathematics courses left out as not spiritual practice.
Sanskrit grammar (Bhooshanasaram) and Abhijnana Shakuntalam lecture series left out as academic.
No free resources on its own site were confirmed (articles are blog posts).
